claims.text: Al0.7CoCrFeNi is a eutectic alloy whose homogenized initial state has a dual-phase FCC/B2 lamellar structure.
The initial FCC/B2 lamellae have incoherent interfaces.
The incoherent interfaces concentrate stress and cause interfacial cracking and brittleness.
The proposed intervention uses a hexahedron-anvil apparatus at approximately 6 GPa and 1473 K for 2 hours.
This HPHT treatment will topologically transform the lamellae into a hierarchically patterned microstructure.
The transformed microstructure will replace incoherent lamellar boundaries with coherent FCC/B2 interfaces.
Coherent interfaces allow dislocations to transfer between the FCC and B2 phases.
Interphase dislocation transfer alleviates the stress concentrations responsible for cracking.
The transformed structure enables stacking-fault formation and twinning in addition to dislocation transfer.
These deformation mechanisms promote homogeneous strain distribution between the FCC and B2 phases.
Homogeneous deformation will effectively arrest interfacial cracking.
The coherent hierarchical structure will enhance ductility without sacrificing strength.
HPHT treatment will simultaneously increase yield strength and elongation to failure relative to the baseline.
The treated alloy's fracture surface will exhibit elongated cracks rather than the isolated microcracks of the baseline.
The GND densities of the FCC and B2 phases will converge at high strain after HPHT treatment.
A pressure-temperature window exists that produces the coherent topological transformation without causing phase decomposition or instability.
Conventional cryo-rolling and annealing will not produce the same hierarchical coherence and GND homogenization as HPHT.
The exact pressure-temperature transformation window may vary with minor compositional fluctuations.
The long-term stability of the proposed coherent interfaces is not characterized.
The individual contributions of dislocation transfer, stacking faults, and twinning may be difficult to quantify.
